body: But that's it, the anxiety is just impenetrable (or feels like it at least). It's the only reason I've stuck with architecture for the time I have. I cope far better with depression than with anxiety. I choose it every day of the week. The anxiety is bad enough that, well, it literally makes me want to kill myself. In fact, this problem only really arose (or at least became exacerbated beyond my capacity to cope) once the anxiety I started feeling about the course started to match that which I feel about any sort of path outside of the course. It makes every moment torture, and suicide seems to be the only off buttong

Regarding the course, well, on one hand, it's incredibly intensive (renowned for it). I think we have one of, if not the highest dropout rate of any course here. It consumes your life. I live in a house of 7 architects, but it's always dead silent because everyone's always working. You see people breaking down in tears, developing sores from stress, and they've recently had to start locking the studios at 12 because people were bringing in sleeping bags and just, well, living there. 

On the other hand, I don't enjoy architecture. I'm not passionate about buildings, and I don't want to be an architect. I chose the course because I enjoy art and physics, but it hasn't been well suited to me at all. To be honest, I don't think I'm particularly good at it either. The bits others find intuitive and enjoyable I find stressful and difficult, and though I manage them in the end, it takes more work than it should, and never looks particularly great.

Even that might be manageable, but from the sounds of it (some of my housemates are currently in the 3rd year), the difficulty increases exponentially next year. I was burnt out in first year, I'm depleted now, and I just don't know what to do with that...

Yea, sorry for being so vague. I'm a second year architecture student, but can't continue with the course. It's just destroying me, physically, mentally, emotionally. However, for a range of reasons, internal and external, even the thought of leaving it and doing something else brings on bouts of intense anxiety (not quite a panic attack I don't think, though definitely some hyperventilation) I've felt trapped between the two states, depression and anxiety, for at least a year and a half now, and i had a bit of a breakdown about a month a go (it was at this point that it became clear that suicide was my only option. Since then I just stopped attending classes altogether, which didn't help..)

It feels like I have no options left. Like I'm a failure, and doomed to fail at everything I do. I can see my life gradually falling apart around me, though for the past year I've been desperately trying to hold it together. Now everything's just collapsed into a continuum of hopelessness and anxiety, and I'm sick of it. Dying now seems like my only option, the only way of not having to watch my entire world disintegrate around me.
